nodes.summary: The law `N(0, v)` reweighted by the density `exp(h x - h² v / 2)` is `N(h v, v)`. For `v = 0` both sides are the Dirac mass at `0`.
nodes.title: Exponential tilting of a centered Gaussian

nodes.summary: Le Cam's first lemma (LAN case). Let `Qₙ = exp(Λₙ) · P` be probability measures. If `Sₙ → N(0, v)` in distribution under `P` and `Λₙ - h Sₙ → -h² v / 2` in `P`-probability, then `Qₙ` is contiguous with respect to `P`. This is the case of Le Cam's first lemma in which `Λₙ → N(-σ²/2, σ²)` under `P`, `σ² = h² v`; the general form (any limit `L` of `dQₙ/dP` with `E L = 1`) is not stated here.
nodes.title: Le Cam's first lemma

nodes.summary: The sequence of measures `Q n` is contiguous with respect to `P n` (`Q ◁ P`): every sequence of measurable sets whose `P n`-measure tends to `0` has `Q n`-measure tending to `0`.
nodes.title: Contiguity of sequences of measures

nodes.summary: Le Cam's third lemma (LAN case). Let `Qₙ = exp(Λₙ) · P` be probability measures. If `Sₙ → N(0, v)` in distribution under `P` and `Λₙ - h Sₙ → -h² v / 2` in `P`-probability, then `Sₙ → N(h v, v)` in distribution under `Qₙ`. This is the case of Le Cam's third lemma for the central sequence itself (covariance `h v` with `Λₙ`); the general form, for an arbitrary statistic jointly asymptotically normal with `Λₙ`, is not…
nodes.title: Le Cam's third lemma

nodes.summary: If `Q ◁ P` (a fixed `P`) and the measurable functions `T n` converge to `c` in `P`-probability, then `Q n {ω | ε ≤ |T n ω - c|} → 0` for every `ε > 0`.
nodes.title: Contiguity transfers convergence in probability
